about: The Ultimate Challenge's own rounds: never played on the Board or in Defuse. Cambridge formats only, written around the traps B2 First actually sets.

rounds.prompt: The suspect is believed ___ the country shortly after the robbery.
rounds.note: An earlier action after a reporting passive: is believed + perfect infinitive (to have left).

rounds.prompt: I'm still not used to ___ what to do by people younger than me.
rounds.note: be used to + -ing, and the meaning is passive (others tell me): being told.

rounds.prompt: The documents need ___ before Friday, or the whole deal falls through.
rounds.note: need + -ing has a passive meaning: the documents need signing (= need to be signed).

rounds.prompt: She hates ___ in public, so please don't mention her award at dinner.
rounds.note: She is the one praised, so the gerund is passive: being praised.

rounds.prompt: During the fire drill we ___ leave the building in under three minutes.
rounds.note: make sb do → be made TO do: the 'to' comes back in the passive. 'Let' has no passive; use 'be allowed to'.

rounds.prompt: The bridge ___ when the earthquake struck, so it never opened.
rounds.note: Work in progress at a past moment, and the bridge doesn't build: past continuous passive.

rounds.prompt: Neither of the stolen paintings ___ since the robbery in 1990.
rounds.note: Since + a past point needs the present perfect, and paintings are recovered by someone: has been recovered.

rounds.prompt: The children were well looked ___ while their parents were working abroad.
rounds.note: A phrasal verb keeps its particle in the passive: look after → be looked after.

rounds.prompt: The manor, ___ in 1820 for a wealthy merchant, is now a hotel.
rounds.note: A reduced relative clause: the manor, (which was) built in 1820. 'Being built' would mean the work is still going on.

rounds.prompt: ___ in a hurry, the report was full of mistakes.
rounds.note: The report didn't write anything; it was written, and before the mistakes were found: having been written.

rounds.prompt: I'd rather not ___ in the middle of a presentation again.
rounds.note: would rather + bare infinitive, here passive: be interrupted.

rounds.prompt: The film is rumoured ___ several times before its release.
rounds.note: Rumoured about an earlier action done TO the film: perfect passive infinitive.

rounds.prompt: The patient shouldn't ___ home so soon — she's back in hospital already.
rounds.note: Criticising a past decision: shouldn't have + been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: This concert hall ___ up to 2,000 people.
rounds.note: 'Hold' meaning 'have room for' is a state verb with no passive. 'Is held' means an event takes place.

rounds.prompt: There ___ to be more than 300 species of bird on the island.
rounds.note: There + be said to be, and the verb agrees with the species: there are said to be.

rounds.prompt: He was seen ___ the bank only minutes before it was robbed.
rounds.note: see sb do → be seen TO do: the 'to' returns in the passive.

rounds.prompt: The museum is closed while the roof ___ being repaired.
rounds.note: Present continuous passive: is being repaired.

rounds.prompt: Much of the damage could have ___ avoided if the warnings had been taken seriously.
rounds.note: Modal perfect passive: could have been avoided.

rounds.prompt: He hates being made fun ___, especially in front of his friends.
rounds.note: make fun of → be made fun of: the preposition stays after the participle.

rounds.prompt: The thief ___ caught on camera, which made him easy to identify.
rounds.note: Past passive with be or get: was / got caught.

rounds.prompt: I really object ___ being treated like a child.
rounds.note: object to + -ing, here with a passive gerund: object to being treated.

rounds.prompt: The building is thought to have ___ designed by one of Gaudí's students.
rounds.note: Reporting passive about the past: is thought to have been designed.

rounds.prompt: None of the money that ___ been donated so far has reached the victims.
rounds.note: Perfect passive in the relative clause: that has been donated.

rounds.prompt: The novel was turned into a film directed ___ a little-known Korean director.
rounds.note: The agent after a past participle: directed by.

rounds.prompt: The suspects are ___ questioned by police at this very moment.
rounds.note: 'At this very moment' needs the present continuous passive: are being questioned.

rounds.prompt: What ___ this bridge made of? It looks as if it could fall down any minute.
rounds.note: In a question the auxiliary moves in front: What is it made of?

rounds.prompt: I'd hate ___ be kept waiting for hours like last time.
rounds.note: would hate + to-infinitive, here passive: to be kept waiting.

rounds.prompt: This problem needs ___ be dealt with before it gets any worse.
rounds.note: need + passive infinitive: needs to be dealt with.

rounds.prompt: Nobody enjoys ___ laughed at, least of all teenagers.
rounds.note: enjoy + -ing, with a passive meaning: being laughed at.

rounds.prompt: The old cinema is going to ___ knocked down and replaced with flats.
rounds.note: going to + passive infinitive: is going to be knocked down.

rounds.prompt: People believe that the fire was started deliberately.
rounds.note: Reporting passive about the past: is believed + to have been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Someone is going to repair our roof next week.
rounds.note: have something done for an arranged service: are having the roof repaired.

rounds.prompt: Nobody told us about the change of plan.
rounds.note: The person told becomes the subject: we were not told about.

rounds.prompt: It's possible that the letter was sent to the wrong address.
rounds.stem: The letter ___ to the wrong address.
rounds.note: Possibility about the past, passive: may have been sent.

rounds.prompt: They should have warned the residents about the flood.
rounds.note: ought to have + been + past participle — a past criticism in the passive.

rounds.prompt: My parents didn't let me go to the concert.
rounds.stem: I ___ to the concert by my parents.
rounds.note: 'Let' has no passive: be allowed to.

rounds.prompt: Nobody has used this room for years.
rounds.note: Present perfect passive with for: has not been used.

rounds.prompt: Somebody broke into our neighbours' house last night.
rounds.note: get something done for something unpleasant that happened to you: got their house broken into.

rounds.prompt: It is said that the director is planning a sequel.
rounds.note: Personal reporting passive with an action in progress: is said to be planning.

rounds.prompt: Experts think that the bridge collapsed because it was poorly maintained.
rounds.stem: The bridge ___ because it was poorly maintained.
rounds.note: Reporting passive about an earlier event: is thought to have collapsed.

rounds.prompt: They will have finished the new stadium by next summer.
rounds.stem: The new stadium ___ by next summer.
rounds.note: Future perfect passive: will have been completed.

rounds.prompt: Someone needs to look at that broken heater.
rounds.note: need + passive infinitive, keeping the preposition: to be looked at.

rounds.prompt: People don't often see snow in this part of the country.
rounds.stem: Snow ___ in this part of the country.
rounds.note: Present simple passive with a frequency adverb: is not often seen.

rounds.prompt: The news surprised everyone.
rounds.note: be taken by surprise / be taken aback by: the people surprised become the subject.

rounds.prompt: My sister did my hair for the party.
rounds.stem: I ___ my sister for the party.
rounds.note: have something done by someone: had my hair done by.

rounds.prompt: The hotel is closed because they are redecorating it at the moment.
rounds.stem: The hotel is closed because it ___ at the moment.
rounds.note: Present continuous passive: is being redecorated.

rounds.prompt: Nobody has given me any information about the delay.
rounds.stem: I ___ any information about the delay.
rounds.note: With two objects, the person becomes the subject: I haven't been given any information.
